name: Stahleck Castle

opening_hours.seasonal_note: The castle operates as a youth hostel; access to grounds and tower is generally open during hostel operating hours.

accessibility: Limited — steep hill path to reach the castle
tagline: A medieval Rhine castle turned youth hostel, commanding the UNESCO gorge above Bacharach
highlights: Part of the UNESCO Upper Middle Rhine Valley
One of the most dramatically positioned castles on the Rhine
Now operates as a youth hostel — you can sleep inside a medieval castle
Sweeping views over the Rhine gorge, vineyards, and Bacharach
Medieval tower, curtain walls, and courtyard well-preserved

description: Burg Stahleck commands one of the most striking positions in the UNESCO-listed Upper Middle Rhine Valley, perched high above the perfectly preserved medieval town of Bacharach and the river gorge below. First documented in 1135, the castle was a Rhenish Palatinate stronghold throughout the medieval period, controlling river traffic through the narrow gorge. Badly damaged in the Thirty Years' War, it was rebuilt in the 1920s–1930s by the German Youth Hostel Association (DJH) and today operates as one of Germany's most spectacular and beloved youth hostels — allowing guests to sleep within authentic medieval walls above the Rhine. The courtyard, tower, and ramparts are freely accessible, offering panoramic views down the gorge.
history: First documented in 1135, the castle was a key Rhenish stronghold controlling Rhine traffic for the Counts Palatine. It was besieged and partially destroyed during the Thirty Years' War (1618–1648) and fell into ruin. The German Youth Hostel movement acquired the ruins in 1925 and undertook a restoration, opening it as a hostel in 1926. It has operated continuously as a hostel since, aside from World War II, and was included in the UNESCO Upper Middle Rhine Valley designation in 2002.
how_to_visit:
**Getting there:** Bacharach is on the west bank of the Rhine, 40 km south of Koblenz. Frequent Rhine Valley trains on the Koblenz–Mainz line stop at Bacharach station; the castle is a 20-minute walk uphill from the station through the medieval town walls. Rhine cruise ships also stop at Bacharach in summer.

**Tickets:** Entry to the castle grounds and tower is free. The castle operates as a youth hostel (Burg Stahleck); overnight stays must be booked directly at burg-stahleck.de.

**Practical tips:** The grounds are accessible during hostel operating hours (07:00–22:00 daily) with no ticket desk or timed entry required. The youth hostel accepts guests of all ages — advance booking is strongly recommended in summer and during wine-harvest weekends.

**Combine with:** [Marksburg Castle](/castles/germany/marksburg-castle), the only Rhine valley castle never destroyed, lies about 25 km north near Braubach and makes a natural same-day pairing. [Stolzenfels Castle](/castles/germany/stolzenfels-castle) near Koblenz is another well-preserved Rhine gorge fortress within easy reach.

faqs.question: Can anyone stay in the youth hostel?
faqs.answer: Yes — Burg Stahleck youth hostel is open to all ages (youth hostels in Germany are not restricted to young people). Advance booking is strongly recommended.

faqs.question: Is the castle part of a UNESCO site?
faqs.answer: Yes — Burg Stahleck is within the Upper Middle Rhine Valley, a UNESCO World Heritage Site recognised for its combination of castles, medieval towns, and vineyards along 65 km of the Rhine gorge.

faqs.question: What is the town of Bacharach like?
faqs.answer: Bacharach is one of the best-preserved medieval towns in the Rhine Valley, with intact 14th-century walls, half-timbered houses, and a Romanesque church — an ideal base for exploring the gorge.

hotel.non_guest_access_note: The castle courtyard, tower and ramparts remain freely accessible to day visitors, whether or not you book a room — see How to Visit above
hotel.how_to_stay:
**Getting there:** Bacharach, Rhineland-Palatinate — same access as described in How to Visit above.

**Rooms & rates:** Private double rooms and multi-bed dormitories are all within the restored medieval castle building itself. From roughly €25-35 per person per night (DJH hostel pricing, not per-room — this is a youth hostel rate, not the per-room-per-night convention used elsewhere on this site), including bedding; breakfast, half-board and full-board options available.

**On-site:** Hostel restaurant/dining hall; the castle courtyard, tower and ramparts described in How to Visit remain freely accessible to both overnight guests and day visitors.

**Good to know:** Open to guests of all ages, not just young people — a genuine budget option for sleeping inside an authentic medieval Rhine castle, a sharp contrast to the luxury positioning of most other castle-hotels covered on this site.

**Combine with:** Marksburg Castle and Stolzenfels Castle, both within easy reach — see the recommendations above.
